RHEUMATOLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-04-28
28M, ambulatory visit for a scheduled rheumatology check-up.

S:
Patient returns for routine rheumatology follow-up. He reports morning stiffness in both hands lasting over an hour, along with swelling and tenderness across the knuckles that makes gripping tools difficult. Symptoms have been worse over the past month despite his current regimen. He works as a warehouse order picker and says the repetitive hand use aggravates the pain. Symptoms limit him to about 2 hours of activity before he needs to rest; he missed 5 shifts last month. Denies chest pain. Sleep is interrupted by hand discomfort. Lives with a roommate. Never smoker, occasional alcohol on weekends.

O:
BP 120/76, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.3 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 165 lb, BMI 24.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
Hands: symmetric swelling and tenderness at the MCP and PIP joints bilaterally, with reduced grip strength.
Wrists: mild warmth, limited flexion.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Labs (this week): ESR 42 mm/hr, CRP elevated, CBC within normal limits, anti-CCP positive on prior testing.

A/P:
1. Rheumatoid arthritis with active synovitis of both hands. Joint activity elevated today. Continue methotrexate weekly with folic acid; discussed escalating therapy and ordered baseline labs for a possible biologic. Reviewed joint protection techniques and referred to occupational therapy for hand splinting.
2. Symptom control: short course of low-dose prednisone to bridge during this flare, with a taper plan. Reinforced the importance of weekly medication adherence and lab monitoring.
3. Function and work: current hand limitations are affecting his ability to keep his usual shifts. Provided a letter outlining activity restrictions for his employer and recommended ergonomic adjustments.

Return to clinic in 6 weeks to reassess joint activity and review labs, sooner if swelling worsens.
